Variable-viscosity vector stress boundary-value problem −∇⋅τ=f,τ=2με(u),ε(u)=12(∇u+∇uT)−∇⋅τ=f,τ=2με(u),ε(u)=21​(∇u+∇uT) 1<r<2,μ=1+r2/5,A=(r2−1)(4−r2),u⋆=A(1+xy,(x2−y2)/2)T1<r<2,μ=1+r2/5,A=(r2−1)(4−r2),u⋆​=A(1+xy,(x2−y2)/2)T ∫Ω2μ ε(uh):ε(vh) dA=∫Ωf⋅vh dA∫Ω​2με(uh​):ε(vh​)dA=∫Ω​f⋅vh​dA Linear stress-divergence BVP coupling two Cartesian components. Q1 basis functions in polar coordinates use the exact curved Jacobian and include variable-mu gradients and shear. There is no pressure,incompressibility constraint or advective term.
